text.p: Jeff Juden has a couple of streaks going -- hitting and pitching.
The Montreal right-hander pitched a four-hitter for his fourth straight win and added a two-run single in the sixth inning to lead the Expos to a 5-2 victory over the Florida Marlins Thursday.

Juden (9-2), who walked two and struck out six, recorded his second complete game of the season and third of his career. Since dropping consecutive outings on May 30 and June 4, he has given up only nine runs and 23 hits in four wins spanning 31 2/3 innings.
"I had a good curveball," said Juden. "I was able to spot my fastball. I had great defence behind me and the guys put runs up for me."
He added: "Hey, I've got a three-game hitting streak."

After Gary Sheffield led off the Marlins' fifth with his eighth home run, Montreal gotm three runs in the sixth. Vladimir Guerrero and Rondell White singled before Chris Widger hit an RBI double and Juden singled in two runs.

"He's a competitor, he's getting better," said Expos manager Felipe Alou of Juden. "His tempo is better, his command is better. He didn't have that in the early going. It was tough to play defence behind him."
Montreal, which snapped a two-game skid, leads the majors with 14 complete games.
Florida starter Pat Rapp (4-5) lost his third straight decision. He gave up five runs, nine hits and three walks with six strikeouts in five-plus innings.
The Marlins had a two-game winning streak halted and lost for just the third time in their last 11 contests.
In Los Angeles, Tony Gwynn hit an inside-the-park grand slam as the San Diego Padres defeated the Dodgers for the seventh straight time, 9-7.

Mark Guthrie (1-2) relieved starter Tom Candiotti to begin the seventh and gave up singles to pinch-hitter Greg Vaughn and Rickey Henderson and a walk to Steve Finley to load the bases. Gwynn lined Guthrie's 1-2 pitch down the line, past diving left fielder Brett Butler, who injured his neck and shoulder.
The ball rolled into the corner and centre fielder Roger Cedeno had to chase it down. Gwynn slid past catcher Mike Piazza ahead of the relay, giving the Padres an 8-4 lead.
Sean Bergman (2-2) allowed four runs and eight hits in six innings for the win. Trevor Hoffman got his 14th save, despite giving up two runs and two hits in 1 2/3 innings.
Finley had a solo homer for San Diego and Piazza hit a two-run shot in the ninth for the Dodgers.
In Atlanta, Denny Neagle pitched eight strong innings for his fourth straight victory and Fred McGriff drove in a pair of runs as the Braves edged the Philadelphia Phillies 5-4.

Neagle (11-1) gave up three runs, seven hits and a walk with seven strikeouts to become the National League's second 11-game winner. He posted his first career victory against Philadelphia in four decisions and 15 appearances.
Atlanta has won five of its last seven games but snapped a five-game home losing skid.
Matt Beech (0-3), trying for the eighth time to post his first win, surrendered five runs, six hits and six walks with six strikeouts in six innings.
The Phillies have dropped three straight, 11 of their last 12 games, and six in a row on the road.

In Chicago, Jeff Bagwell's one-out single in the top of the 10th -- the fourth in a row in the inning off reliever Terry Adams (1-4) -- scored Thomas Howard with the go-ahead run as the Houston Astros edged the Cubs 7-6.
The Cubs rallied to tie the game in the bottom of the ninth when Mark Grace delivered an RBI double off Billy Wagner (4-3), who suffered his third blown save but got the win.

Craig Biggio hit a two-run homer and Brad Ausmus added a solo shot for the Astros, who have won five of their last seven games. Blas Minor pitched the 10th for his first save since August 1995 as a member of the Mets.
In Cincinnati, Delino DeShields drove in two runs, including a sacrifice fly that snapped a sixth-inning tie, as the St Louis Cardinals defeated the Reds 5-3.
Todd Stottlemyre (6-5) allowed three runs and four hits over five innings to defeat the Reds for the second time in six days.
Dennis Eckersley allowed one hit in a scoreless ninth for his 15th save of the season and 368th of his career, moving past Jeff Reardon into second place on the all-time list.
It was also the 988th appearance by Eckersley, moving him past Lindy McDaniel for fourth place on the all-time games pitched list.
Dave Burba (4-8) took the loss.
At Colorado, Ellis Burks's RBI single snapped a tie and keyed a four-run sixth inning that gave the Rockies a 7-6 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
